small_guidance:
- Add larger N-dim tiles to the autotune list (e.g. `BLOCK_M=128, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32` at `num_warps=8, num_stages=2`, and `BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=128, BLOCK_K=32`) — current best likely picks a 16-K tile and OC=128 maps perfectly to BLOCK_N=128, eliminating the OC-mask overhead.
- Swap the program-id mapping so `pid_sp` varies fastest within an N (i.e. `program_id(0)=spatial`, `program_id(1)=n*oc_tiles+oc_tile`) and add an L2 swizzle (group_size_m ~ 8) to improve weight-tile reuse across spatial tiles for the same (N, OC).
- Hoist the `ic/kh/kw` decomposition: since `IC*KH*KW = 576` is small, fully unroll the K loop (`BLOCK_K=32`, 18 iters) and precompute `ih/iw` from `oh,ow` once outside the loop, only updating `kh,kw` per iter — reduces integer divmod cost.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM with input loaded in NHWC (channels_last). Permute x to `(N, H, W, IC)` once at module init/forward entry; the K-axis (IC*KH*KW) then walks IC as the innermost contiguous dim, giving fully coalesced 128-byte loads per BLOCK_K step instead of the current strided gather across `stride_xc = H*W = 16384`.
- Make the kernel persistent over output channels for a fixed (N, spatial-tile): load the spatial input patch slab once into registers/SMEM and sweep all OC tiles, fusing ReLU+bias in the epilogue. With OC=128 and IC*KH*KW=576, one spatial tile's input footprint dominates; reusing it across OC eliminates the redundant x-loads currently done per OC tile.
- Consider splitting the K-reduction across kh*kw (9 iters) at the outer level and keeping IC as the inner BLOCK_K — this lets you hoist `ih,iw` computation entirely out of the inner loop and keeps `tl.dot` operating on a clean `[BM, IC] @ [IC, BN]` GEMM with no index arithmetic inside.
